note: Inputs to the cost-of-poverty estimate (optionb_report.py, section 8b). Every external figure was seen only in search results or secondary coverage: the primary sources could not be opened from the drafting environment, so each needs checking before submission. 'assumption' marks a value chosen here.

ncoss.source: NCOSS and Impact Economics and Policy, Lasting Impacts: the economic costs of child poverty in NSW, November 2024; the lower of the two direct-cost figures published (A$25bn and A$26bn) is used

causal_share_low.basis: assumption: half of the direct costs avoidable by income alone (quasi-experimental effects of US$1,000 a year of 2 to 6% of a standard deviation in test scores; no study gives a single share)

adult_health_premium.basis: assumption, bounded by the AIHW ratios of the lowest to the highest socioeconomic group: disease burden 1.6 times (2018), potentially preventable hospitalisations 1.7 times (2022-23)

uprate.basis: wage growth in the 2026-27 Budget parameters (the paper's 3.5% a year)

benchmarks.scope: child poverty: lost earnings, health, crime, homelessness, maltreatment

benchmarks.study: Holzer, Schanzenbach, Duncan and Ludwig (2007), United States
benchmarks.scope: child poverty: lost output, crime, health
child poverty: public services, lost earnings and taxes; no health loss valued

benchmarks.study: Bramley, Hirsch, Littlewood and Watkins (2016), United Kingdom
benchmarks.scope: poverty at all ages: public services (£69bn, about £1 in every £5 of public service spending) and lost taxes and extra benefits (£9bn)
